observation.visible_scene: A backlit silhouette of a long-haired figure performing expressive dance movements in a hazy, purple-lit space. Two horizontal neon bars sit low on the left (a blue glow pools behind them) and two on the right, all remaining fixed in the frame. Thick smoke/fog fills the background, tinted magenta and violet with a cooler blue region on the left.
visible_changes: At the start (t~0-0.17s) the figure's arms are bent with hands held close to the torso and hair falling to the right.
Over t~0.25-0.6s both arms unfold outward to the sides into a wide, near-horizontal extension.
Through t~0.7-1.1s the arms stay spread wide while the torso and head sway and tilt, and the hair shifts side to side.
Around t~1.2-1.5s the arms draw back inward, one hand returning toward the chest.
From t~1.5-2.1s one arm lifts upward and arcs overhead while the body leans.
During t~2.2-2.6s that raised arm sweeps across the top of the frame and descends toward a horizontal position.
By t~2.7-3.3s both arms are again extended outward horizontally, hands open, with the figure swaying.
The neon bars and the overall purple/blue lighting remain in constant positions throughout; the drifting smoke subtly changes texture but no bar moves or changes color.
The figure's silhouette (curly long hair, cropped top, fitted lower garment) persists unchanged in identity across the excerpt.
outside_clip_unknowns: What triggered or preceded the dance motion before t=0, and how the movement resolves after t=3.33s.
Whether the segment is part of a continuous performance or one phrase of a longer routine.
The dancer's facing, expression, and exact body orientation, hidden by the silhouette lighting.
uncertain_details: Any slight camera drift is indeterminate because the static neon bars give no clear parallax evidence; background is treated as fixed.
Motion blur on the limbs at several frames makes precise hand/finger positions ambiguous.
The left/right assignment of the raised arm is inferred from the viewer's perspective and may reflect the dancer's own left or right arm.
